standard: Visible refinement acceptable at application scale; not a numerical quality score or release approval.

front.note: The spun shade now has a smooth continuous contour above the articulated brass arm, improving the coarse original silhouette.

rear.note: The shade and twin arm bars remain distinct and connected to the circular wall plate; the upper neck opening is retained.

detail.note: The close view shows an even cone rim and neck transition without radial faceting or a collapsed tip.

underside.note: The open lower shade exposes the intended warm diffuser and a continuous inner rim; arm joints remain seated.

clay.note: The untextured view confirms that the smoother hollow shade is real construction, with the authored arm pose and mount preserved.

front.note: The circular top, fluted tapered pedestal and stepped foot now form one visibly supported table with smooth turned outlines.

rear.note: The rear preserves the same continuous fluted construction and seated top, without a floating cap or uneven base.

detail.note: The flutes terminate consistently at the upper support and lower collar, retaining the original blue and white material separation.

underside.note: The full-size underside shows the pedestal meeting the top cleanly, with a closed circular foot and no inherited support gap.

clay.note: The clay view confirms the smooth turned top and base profiles and dense, regular authored flutes.

front.note: The compact cooker now has a smooth round body and fitted lid, with the small front display retained.

rear.note: The back is a continuous closed appliance shell with aligned lid and lower trim, improving the original faceted cylinder.

detail.note: The pressure vent sits on the lid and the fine grip marks wrap the top knob correctly; neither detail floats above the surface.

underside.note: A closed dark base and continuous lower rim are visible, with the display attached to the body.

clay.note: The clay view confirms rounded manufactured body and lid contours with separate vent and knob construction.

front.note: The six globes sit on a continuous smooth brass ring with the original three-point suspension and canopy retained.

rear.note: The ring remains even from the opposite direction, without the former overlapping tapered end seam.

detail.note: The close view shows a rounded uninterrupted ring surface and thin suspension wires meeting the authored frame.

underside.note: The underside exposes a continuous closed tube and seated globe stems, with no doubled end caps.

clay.note: The clay view confirms the clean toroidal silhouette and original globe spacing independently of metallic highlights.

front.note: The steel case reads as a smooth satin housing around the retained layered dial; the false coarse checker grain is gone.

rear.note: Compared with the prior full-size rear render, the hemispherical case now has continuous reflections instead of golf-ball-like repeating bumps.

detail.note: The full-size view retains the dial lettering, hour markers, hands and date window while restoring smooth original steel; small inherited bezel facets remain acceptable at application scale.

underside.note: The lower view preserves the distinct bezel and readable dial against the continuous steel hemisphere, without added grain or changed colors.

clay.note: The clay view confirms the original case geometry and layered clock mechanism remain intact; this correction restores the authored surface rather than claiming new geometric detail.
